actions.action: Move the pot out of direct afternoon sun into shade
Move the pot under cover for rain protection
Scratch-test stems to see if they are alive
Prune dead wood back to green tissue, no more than a third of the plant
Check soil with a finger and water when the top 1-2 inches are dry, letting it drain fully
Get a fast-draining mix (potting mix with perlite or grit, or amended succulent soil)
Repot into a pot slightly larger than the root ball, loosening the outer roots and not burying the crown, now or after the heat passes

reason: The answer blames earlier overwatering and mentions terracotta drying only as a secondary swing. It never suggests a plastic pot or more water, instead stressing drying out between waterings. That safeguarded soil-check advice is unhelpful rather than harmful.
